chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from Al-A'mash, from Abu Wael, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: When the Mahdi was mentioned: 'Indeed, he will be given allegiance between the Rukn and the Maqam. His name is Ahmad, Abdullah, and Al-Mahdi; these are his three names.'

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ: Ahmad, one of the names of the Mahdi
key_terms.الرُّكْنُ: The Rukn, a specific corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Guided One, a title for the twelfth Imam
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: Abdullah, one of the names of the Mahdi
key_terms.وَالْمَقَامُ: And the Maqam, the station of Abraham near the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What are the three names of Imam Mahdi mentioned in this hadith and where will his allegiance take place?
ai.summary: This narration from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the prophetic precedent for the Mahdi’s public allegiance in Mecca, specifically between the Rukn and Maqam, highlighting his dual identity as both 'Ahmad' (echoing the Prophet) and 'Abdullah' (Servant of God). The inclusion of these three names underscores his legitimacy within the Ahl al-Bayt lineage and his role as the eschatological restorer of justice, a theme central to Twelver Shia eschatology.
